To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the C-ter-minal region of the InsP3 receptor is important for the regulation of Ca2+ release and InsP3 binding, and that the C-termination of the InsP receptor is exposed to cytoplasmic surface of endoplasmic recticulum.
the Ins(1)P3 receptor contains a region that is exposed to the luminal surface of the smooth endosome reticulum and which is involved in both binding of Ins(1) P3 and gating of Ca2+ release channels.
the Ins(1.4,5) receptor is a protein of 300 kDa and has an intraluminal C-terminus, which is essential for Ca(2+) release.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanism of Ca(2+) release through the Ins(1.4.5)P3 receptors.
the molecular mechanism of Ca2+ release by Ins(1, 4, 5)P3.
the role of the Ins( 1,4 5 ) P3 receptor in Ca2+-induced Ca2+ release and the involvement of its C-terminus in the regulation of Ca2+ release activity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Ins(1)4,5P(3)-gated channel is a protein complex of the Ins(4,5) P(3) receptor and a protein(s) that interacts directly with the Ins(4) P(3)-binding domain of the Ins(3,4,5)-P(3) receptor.
the C-terminal region is involved in the regulation of Ca2+ release and that the N-terminal region may be involved in the regulation or stabilization of Ins(1,4,5) P3 binding.
the C- and N-termini are both involved in the regulation of the channel, but the C-termini play the most crucial role.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Ins(1.4,5) P3 receptor is composed of two functional domains, an N-terminal domain for Ins(1, 4,5)IP3 binding, and a C-terminal domain for channel gating.
the C-terminal region is involved in the regulation of Ca2+ release by Ins(1, 4,5) P3.
the C-terminal portion of Ins(1)4,5)3 receptor is a key region for the regulation of Ca2+ release.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the C-terminal domain of the receptor, not the N-terminal domain, plays a role in Ca2+ channel gating.
the InsP3 receptor C terminus is exposed to the lumen of the ER, and that it plays a key role in the gating of the channel.
the C-terminal region plays a critical role in the gating of the channel, but not in Ins(1, 4, 5)P3 recognition.
